label: copy phase of long sequences, early-middle recall (orig tokens 2-4) and final steps of L=9, on a subset of letters
explanation: Active only in the copy phase (never during original input or at <DEL>) and almost only for long sequences (L>=7; L=9 has 64% of mass). Within copy it peaks when recalling original tokens 2-4 (t=10-13) and again at the last two steps of L=9 sequences (t=16-17). It also depends on the input token: high rates for f, v, w, k, a, n, j, d, z, h (and somewhat e, m, r, u, y); it almost never fires when the input is a digit or g, l, o, q, t, x. Never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1), which follows since copy inputs repeat original tokens. The position x token-set predicate gets F1 about 0.6 on dev; the rest of the variance in whether it fires and how strongly is not captured, and I did not characterise magnitude beyond those position and token preferences.
